scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): a two-view response that leans toward welfare while granting that achievements form part of greatness; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: People often disagree about what truly makes a nation great.
Some claim a nation's greatness shows in the achievements of its rulers, artists, and scientists, while others argue it shows in the general welfare of all its people.
I lean toward the second view, but I believe a nation's achievements still form part of its greatness.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why welfare is the surest sign

sentences.text: First, the welfare of all the people is the surest sign of a nation's greatness.
A country that keeps its citizens healthy, safe, and free has succeeded at its most basic task.
For example, a nation with grand achievements but widespread poverty has failed the very people it serves.
This shows that greatness must be felt in ordinary lives, not only at the top.
Welfare touches everyone, while famous achievements may benefit only a fortunate few.
A government that serves all its people has fulfilled its deepest purpose.
For these reasons, I find the second view more convincing.
Second, however, the first view rightly reminds us that achievements also matter.
Great works of art and science can lift a whole people and improve their lives.
Consider how scientific discoveries cure disease, or how great art gives a nation pride and meaning.
Such achievements are often a source of welfare rather than a rival to it.
A nation that nurtures talent usually grows stronger and more prosperous as a result.
Achievement and welfare, in truth, are deeply connected.
Both views, then, capture part of what real greatness means.
In conclusion, I believe a nation's greatness is best measured by the welfare of all its people.
But its achievements matter too, since they often raise that welfare and enrich its culture.
A truly great nation turns its finest achievements toward the good of every citizen.
